correctness.rationale: All possibilities of the independent directed Bernoulli update are enumerated. Conditional non-null moves are unbiased dyadic half-interval transitions with stopping probability \(s_k=q_k/(2-q_k)\); this yields the complete atomic law, finite stopping, and exact moment/holding-time identities. The coupling to a uniform point in the selected dyadic interval establishes weak convergence, and countable-vs-atomless support gives total-variation distance one. Bounding the expected number of stages by \(O(\log(d/arepsilon))\) and later waiting by \(1/h_1\) establishes the sharp time constant. The standalone rational verifier checks independent finite transition trees and 3 logistic parameter samples; the infinite proof is analytic.

value.rationale: The quantity being classified is the full terminal opinion distribution, a natural observable absent from the motivating simulation study. A singular limit converts a countable atomic consensus measure into uniform weak law while total variation remains one; the exact inverse-width exponential mean time explains apparent polarization in finite runs. The coupled law and time scale provide a substantive model-specific benchmark for interpreting rare-interaction simulations and identifying stochastic opinion uncertainty, beyond an elementary qualitative convergence assertion.
